# Apply for a Small Business Grant

Share: [![Shopping Cart Icon](https://www.miamidade.gov/resources/images/social-icons/Social-Media-Facebook.png)](https://www.miamidade.gov/global/service.page?Mduid_service=ser1471548035447835# "Share on Facebook") [![Shopping Cart Icon](https://www.miamidade.gov/resources/images/social-icons/Social-Media-X.png)](https://www.miamidade.gov/global/service.page?Mduid_service=ser1471548035447835# "Twitter")

The Small Business Grant Program offers funding opportunities for small owned and operated businesses to purchase equipment, supplies, advertising/marketing, inventory, building liability insurance, security systems and to make minor renovations.

- All businesses must be located in the specified county commission district
- Must be a for-profit business
- Must not be part of a national chain
- A physical address is required
- Supporting documentation must be provided (W-9, Municipal Local Business Tax Certificate, any applicable licenses, etc.)
- Home-based businesses can apply

Additional criteria may be required, based on commission district. Review the guidelines section of the application.

# Miami Open for Business

**Miami Open for Business was a pandemic-era initiative made possible by a $20 million grant from Wells Fargo.** The pandemic laid bare the inequities that exist in small business entrepreneurship: while minorities and women are creating and growing businesses at a faster rate than their peers, they tend to have lower revenue and receive fewer loan approvals, among other challenges, all of which were worsened by the pandemic.

For this reason, Wells Fargo poured back into small businesses in five key cities across the country, including Miami – creating Miami Open for Business. Launched in 2022, this program had an explicit focus on asset-building and asset ownership to make small businesses (and nonprofits, which were also eligible to benefit from the program) more resilient and capable of building generational wealth.

## The Miami Open for Business Approach

The program prioritized small business owners and nonprofit leaders in specific Miami communities that have been historically overlooked and underinvested. We developed two core ways to serve them: by providing financing and technical assistance.

![Miami Open for Business](https://miamifoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Miami_OFB_Logo_BlkGrn.png)

A grant of up to $20,000 that allowed entrepreneurs to invest in their business through the purchase of a technology asset or a piece of equipment, such as a pizza oven or pedicure chair.

### Asset Building Loan for Entrepreneurs (ABLE)

A low-interest loan of up to $100,000 that helped businesses and nonprofits buy inventory or a vehicle, remodel their property, or refinance predatory debt, among other purposes. Repayments will allow initial grant funds to be recycled into future community development projects.

### Collective Real Estate Ownership (CREO)

A fully forgivable loan of up to $500,000 to help small business owners and nonprofit leaders make a down payment on commercial real estate in a historically underinvested community. Properties had to be held in a collective ownership model with another business or organization to spur shared equity.

## Technical Assistance

Miami Open for Business also empowered entrepreneurs with knowledge. Nearly $2 million was used to build a community of technical assistance providers across target communities in Miami who helped businesses apply for financing, organize their books, better understand marketing, and more. Technical assistance providers collectively provided over 1,300 businesses with more than 15,000 hours of assistance. **Roll over the logos to see which neighborhoods these providers served.**

Outside of the technical assistance program, Miami Open for Business also hosted a series of small business workshops, including what is understood to be South Florida’s first-ever commercial real estate first-time buyer workshop.

### The Lessons Learned – And Opportunities Recognized:

1. **We learned the importance of providing culturally appropriate technical assistance,** which is necessary to overcome digital and financial literacy challenges, along with language and cultural barriers.
2. **We learned the importance of working with trusted community-based partners**; support is more accessible when it’s decentralized, and trusted partners helped us be nimbler and more innovative.
3. **We recognized the challenges of navigating commercial real estate**, specifically the limited options for financial support.
4. **We see an opportunity to build a regional philanthropic impact investing alliance** where financial resources can be pooled in support of community development projects.

# **Investing in Small Businesses: Miami Beach’s New Grant Program Offers Up to $5,000**

Running a small business comes with its fair share of successes, challenges, rising operational costs, market competition, and seasonal fluctuations. Miami Beach small businesses are not just a part of the economy, they are the heart of the community. Accordingly, the Small Business Grant Program is designed to provide direct financial support to local businesses working hard to grow and succeed.

The program offers grants of up to $5,000. This is a valuable opportunity for business owners to enhance their operations, support job growth, and build long-term sustainability. For many, this may mean upgrading equipment, expanding marketing efforts, or simply reinforcing the foundation that keeps a business thriving.

The program’s simple application process is first-come, first- funded. Now is the time for eligible businesses to take advantage of this opportunity before the April 14, 2025 deadline.

**Who Can Apply?**

To be eligible for the Small Business Grant Program, businesses must meet the following criteria:

- **Location and Operation**: Must be located within Miami Beach and have a valid **Business Tax Receipt (BTR)** for at least two years.
- **Business Registration**: Must be registered as an active entity with the **Florida Division of Corporations**.
- **Independence**: The business cannot be affiliated with a national chain or franchise.
- **Good Standing**: Businesses must be compliant with all City of Miami Beach and Miami-Dade County regulations, with no outstanding debts, taxes, or code violations.

A complete list of requirements is available at [**Small Business Grant - City of Miami Beach**](https://www.miamibeachfl.gov/business/doing-business-with-mb/business-incentives/small-business-grant/)

**A Bold Move for Your Business**

For many small businesses, a modest financial boost can be a game-changer. Whether it is to purchase new equipment, hire additional staff, or increase marketing efforts, the **Small Business Grant Program** provides a **meaningful opportunity to invest in the future**.

With applications open until **April 14, 2025**,  businesses are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

If you’ve applied to national grants before, Florida’s state-level programs may surprise you. They’re often more specialized, regionally focused, and tied directly to Florida’s economic and community development goals. Are legally registered and incorporated in the state (LLC, S-corp, etc.) - Hold a current business license and are in good standing with the Department of State - Operate primarily within Florida — some grants specify physical location or even ZIP code-based priority zones For example, the City of Tampa’s Relief Fund gives preference to businesses in historically underfunded communities. ### Disqualifiers: Who Likely Won’t Qualify Unfortunately, some businesses won’t meet eligibility no matter how strong the idea. **Common disqualifiers include:** - These grants don’t require repayment and often prioritize innovation, inclusion, and regional economic impact. ### Best Free Grants for Florida Startups in 2025–2026 The following table highlights grants that either explicitly target startups or frequently fund early-stage businesses in Florida: Grant Name Provider Amount Startup Focus [Miami-Dade Mom and Pop Small Business Grant](https://www.miamidade.gov/global/service.page?Mduid_service=ser1471548035447835) Miami-Dade County Up to $5,000 Local startups [FAU Tech Runway Launch Competition](https://www.fau.edu/therunway/) Florida Atlantic University $15,000 + resources Tech/startup accelerator Veteran Florida Entrepreneurial Program Florida SBDC Mentorship + up to $10,000 Veteran-led startups [Cartier Women’s Initiative](https://www.cartierwomensinitiative.com/) Cartier Foundation $30,000 – $100,000 Women-led startups ### What Makes a Grant “Free”? The Comcast team helped redesign our website and offered SEO services for free.”_ — Latina-owned business in Orlando (via Hello Alice community post) ### Florida-Based Grants for Women and Minority Entrepreneurs Helpful Tip Be ready to provide documentation proving: - Demographic ownership (e.g., minority status, gender ID, veteran documentation) - Community benefit (if applicable) - Use of funds and long-term impact Next, we’ll explore which industries are prioritized for Florida business grants in 2025–2026. ## **What industries are prioritized for Florida business grants in 2025–2026?** Not every Florida business qualifies for the same pool of funding — and that’s by design. The state strategically steers its grant funding toward sectors that support job creation, sustainability, technological innovation, and infrastructure. Whether you're building electric delivery trucks or launching a neighborhood café, your industry plays a huge role in whether you'll be prioritized for funding in 2025–2026. ### Florida’s Top Priority Sectors for Grant Funding According to the [Florida Department of Economic Opportunity](https://floridajobs.org/) and Enterprise Florida, the following industries are expected to remain high-priority for public and private grants in the next cycle: “The state’s future funding incentives are increasingly tied to resilience, skilled workforce development, and technological transformation.” ### Industry-Specific Incentive Programs (Examples) - **SBIR/STTR Innovation Grants** — Tech and R&D-focused businesses can apply for up to $250,000 (Phase I) and $1M+ (Phase II). - **Florida High-Tech Corridor Grants** — For businesses in aerospace, defense, and clean tech partnering with universities. - **USDA Energy Efficiency Grants** — Available to agricultural or rural businesses investing in sustainable operations. - **Workforce Training Grants** — Offered to logistics, healthcare, and food service companies hiring and training new workers. ### Tips for Industry-Aligned Applications 1. **Use the same language** as the grant provider: If the grant mentions “resiliency,” “job creation,” or “clean infrastructure,” echo that in your proposal. 2. **Show industry-specific metrics**, such as CO2 reduction (green energy), employee training programs (restaurants), or innovation benchmarks (tech). 3. **Bundle local and federal programs** if your industry qualifies — e.g., use a USDA grant with a city startup grant. ### Are You Outside These Industries? If your business doesn’t fall into a priority industry — don’t panic. Many grants are open-ended or based on community impact, rather than sector. And of course, if you don’t qualify for a grant but still need to grow... **Magenta is built for real-world businesses**— restaurants, cleaners, truckers, freelancers — who are earning $15,000+/month and need fast access to business funding. No credit score required. [Apply here](https://app.magentafunding.com/start-here) — _you can count on us._ ## **How can LLCs and self-employed individuals qualify for Florida business funding?** LLCs and self-employed entrepreneurs — including freelancers, consultants, and gig workers — often wonder whether they’re eligible for small business grants or funding. The good news: yes, many Florida grant programs do accept solo-owned businesses and single-member LLCs. However, your success depends on your structure, documentation, and how you present your case. ### Are LLCs Eligible for Florida Business Grants? Yes. Whether you're a single-member LLC or multi-member entity, you may qualify for local, state, and federal grant programs, provided that: - You are **registered and active in the State of Florida** (via Sunbiz) - You have a **valid EIN (Employer Identification Number)** - You maintain a **business checking account** - You can show **income/revenue history** (even if modest) According to [Florida SBDC](https://floridasbdc.org/category/startup/), "Even solo LLCs and part-time consultants can be eligible for state and federal funding as long as they’re properly registered and structured for commercial activity." Many grant programs don’t ask about the number of employees — they ask for impact, clarity, and plan. ### What About Sole Proprietors or Self-Employed Founders? You can still qualify for business grants as a self-employed individual, especially if you: - Have been operating for at least 6–12 months - Have verifiable income through bank statements or 1099s - Work in a qualifying field (tech, transportation, arts, etc.) - File a Schedule C on your tax return (proof of business income) Freelancers and 1099 workers in Florida became especially eligible for recovery grants in 2020–2022. Now, some counties (like Miami-Dade and Hillsborough) have rolled over these models into broader microenterprise grant programs. ## Grants and Programs That Accept Self-Employed or LLC Applicants Program Name Accepts LLCs? Accepts Self-Employed? Notes [Nav Small Business Grant](https://www.nav.com/resource/small-business-grants/) ![comptab-yes-icon](https://273774.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/273774/act3/images/comptab-yes-icon.svg) ![comptab-yes-icon](https://273774.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/273774/act3/images/comptab-yes-icon.svg) Quarterly grant for any registered business with a bank account [Amber Grant](https://ambergrantsforwomen.com/) ![comptab-yes-icon](https://273774.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/273774/act3/images/comptab-yes-icon.svg) ![comptab-yes-icon](https://273774.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/273774/act3/images/comptab-yes-icon.svg) Especially favorable for women freelancers and solo businesses [Comcast RISE](https://www.comcastrise.com/) ![comptab-yes-icon](https://273774.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/273774/act3/images/comptab-yes-icon.svg) ![comptab-yes-icon](https://273774.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/273774/act3/images/comptab-yes-icon.svg) Includes services (media, marketing) for single-owner businesses [SBA Microloan Program](https://www.sba.gov/funding-programs/loans/microloans) ![comptab-yes-icon](https://273774.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/273774/act3/images/comptab-yes-icon.svg) ![comptab-yes-icon](https://273774.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/273774/act3/images/comptab-yes-icon.svg) Loans but often paired with technical assistance for solo owners ### Tips for Solo Entrepreneurs Applying for Grants - Separate personal and business finances. Always apply from a business account. - Track all income, even part-time work — grant agencies often ask for 3–6 months of revenue history. - Use business planning tools (SCORE or SBDC) to show you’re growth-focused. - Register for certifications (e.g., Women-Owned Business, Minority-Owned) if applicable. ## **Can I get both a grant and a loan for my Florida small business?** Yes — and in many cases, **combining a grant with a loan is a strategic way to grow faster** while maintaining financial flexibility. These two funding types serve different purposes, and using both can strengthen your capital position, especially if your grant is project-based and your loan supports day-to-day operations. ### Grants vs. Loans: A Quick Refresher Aspect Grant Loan Repayment ![comptab-no-icon](https://273774.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/273774/act3/images/comptab-no-icon.svg) Yes (with interest) Source Government, nonprofit, corporate Bank, SBA, online lenders Eligibility Often competitive, mission-aligned Based on revenue, credit, time in business Timeline 30 – 90 days (average) As fast as 1–7 days Usage Usually restricted to specific projects Broad (working capital, payroll, expansion) **Bottom line:** Grants are great for boosting innovation or covering specific needs. Loans provide consistent, scalable funding when time and flexibility matter. ### Can You Combine the Two? Absolutely. Many small businesses in Florida pursue grants first, then supplement their operations with a short-term or SBA-backed loan. The opposite is also common: some use a loan to build momentum (e.g., hire staff or launch marketing), then apply for grants once they can show traction. ### Hybrid Funding in Action: A Florida Case Example Let’s look at a real-world program: **Florida Job Growth Grant Fund + SBA Microloan** - A construction business in Tampa applied for the Florida [Job Growth Grant Fund](https://floridajobs.org/jobgrowth) to support infrastructure improvements. - They paired it with a $50,000 SBA [Microloan](https://www.sba.gov/funding-programs/loans/microloans) to cover equipment costs and pay seasonal employees. - Result: They completed the grant-funded project and used loan repayment as a growth engine, increasing local hiring. ### How to Build a Dual Strategy If you want to use both grants and loans for your business, consider this step-by-step: 1. **Use the grant for high-visibility impact projects** (like tech upgrades or job creation) 2. **Use the loan for recurring or urgent needs** (like vendor payments or payroll) 3. **Separate your expenses** — this improves reporting and IRS compliance 4. **Track your ROI** — if your grant drives growth, you may qualify for better loan terms ### Programs That Blend Grant + Loan Support Program Name Type Details [Florida Job Growth Grant Fund](https://www.floridajobs.org/job-growth-grant-fund) Grant Public infrastructure and workforce development [SBA Microloan Program](https://www.sba.gov/funding-programs/loans/microloans) Loan $500–$50,000, often used by startups and rural firms Enterprise Florida Export Assistance Hybrid Export grant + low-interest export loans ## **How long does it take to receive funds after winning a Florida business grant?** Winning a business grant is a major milestone — but the wait isn’t over just because you’ve been approved. The timeline from acceptance to fund disbursement varies depending on the grant provider, documentation quality, and post-award requirements. In Florida, this window typically ranges 3 months. ### Average Disbursement Timelines by Grant Type Grant Source Approval to Disbursement Time Notes Local (City/County) 2 months Usually faster, especially for COVID-related or microgrant programs State (FL DEO, Enterprise Florida) 3 months Includes verification and budget review phases Federal (SBA, USDA, DOE) 5 months Often requires pre-award compliance review Private/Foundation Grants 2 months Depends on grantor’s internal process, may include interviews or onboarding ### Key Factors That Affect Disbursement Speed 1. **Document Readiness** If you delay submitting post-approval items like a W-9, voided check, or signed grant agreement, your payment can be delayed. 2. **Bank Verification** Funds are often released via ACH, and mismatched bank details can hold things up. 3. **Grant Type & Fiscal Year** State and federal grants tied to a fiscal calendar (e.g., October–September) may not release funds until the next budget cycle opens. 4. **Milestone-Based Payouts** Some grants (especially workforce or infrastructure) pay in phases — e.g., 50% up front, 50% after proof of execution. In most cases, you can expect to receive your Florida business grant funds within 2 – 5 months after approval, with many state programs landing around the 3-month mark. The more complete and accurate your documentation and the faster you respond to any follow-up requests the smoother and quicker the disbursement process will be, regardless of whether your grant is local, state, federal, or from a private foundation. ## **Conclusion: Which Florida grants are right for your small business in 2025–2026?** Choosing the right small business grant isn’t about luck — it’s about alignment. With so many options available across Florida, understanding your industry, business structure, ownership demographics, and growth plans will help you narrow your options effectively. ### Summary Table: Best Florida Grants by Business Type Business Type Recommended Grants Notes New/Startup Florida High-Tech Corridor Matching Grant, Amber Grant for Women Early-stage and low-barrier options Women-Owned Amber Grant, Office of Supplier Diversity Programs Focused on female entrepreneurship Minority-Owned MBDA Grants, OSD Supplier Diversity Targeted support for underrepresented groups LLC/Self-Employed SBA Microgrants, USDA Rural Business Dev Accessible to freelancers and consultants Tech/Green/Trucking SBIR/STTR, DEO Resiliency Grants Innovation-driven sectors prioritized If your business doesn’t meet government grant criteria — maybe it’s too new, too niche, or you’ve been denied — Magenta can help with flexible business funding. With over 1 year in business, $15,000 monthly revenue, and a business checking account, you’re eligible. No minimum FICO. [Apply today — _you can count on us._](https://app.magentafunding.com/start-here) ### Final Tips Before You Apply - Use the [Florida SBDC Network](https://floridasbdc.org/) for one-on-one help - Check Grants.gov and SBA.gov weekly for open federal/state listings - Don’t forget county and city programs — many open quietly each quarter - Track deadlines, and always customize your application to match the grant’s mission Whether you’re just starting or scaling fast, there’s a Florida grant program that aligns with your path. But if you don’t quite qualify — or you need cash flow now — **Magenta is always here to support Florida’s small business growth.** ## **Florida Small Business Grants 2025 – 2026 FAQs** Can I use a Florida grant to pay off existing business debt? Most Florida small business grants cannot be used to pay off existing debts like credit cards or loans. These funds are generally earmarked for growth, innovation, or community impact. Always check the “allowable use of funds” section in the grant guidelines. Are there grants for small businesses operating from home in Florida? Yes, some grants, especially city-level or microenterprise programs, do accept home-based businesses. However, you may need to show a separate business bank account, zoning compliance, or licensure. Be prepared to prove economic activity beyond your residential space. Do Florida grants cover marketing and branding expenses? Some grants include marketing under eligible expenses, particularly those aimed at tourism, digital expansion, or minority business growth. You will often need to include a marketing plan and explain how it supports your business impact. State-level grants may prioritize more infrastructure-focused use. Are there grants available for businesses recovering from natural disasters in Florida? Florida offers recovery grants through state agencies or the SBA when areas are declared disaster zones. These are time-sensitive and often tied to FEMA declarations. They can help with physical damage, temporary closures, or inventory loss. Can nonprofits in Florida apply for small business grants? Certain Florida grants are available to nonprofits, especially those with economic development, workforce training, or innovation missions. However, eligibility varies by funder and not all business grants apply to nonprofits. Check for designations like 501(c)(3) and community partnership requirements. Are there grants for veteran-owned businesses in Florida? Several grants and technical assistance programs are geared toward veteran entrepreneurs. These are often supported by federal or state partnerships or local Chambers of Commerce. You may need DD-214 documentation and a majority veteran ownership stake. Are franchise businesses eligible for Florida grants? Franchises are sometimes eligible, but it depends on whether your business is independently owned and operated. Grants that favor local economic development may exclude national chains or heavily branded entities. It is best to apply through grants that explicitly allow franchises. Can I apply for multiple Florida grants at the same time? In most cases you can apply for several grants simultaneously. Just make sure that you do not request duplicate funding for the same activity or expense. Some grants may require you to disclose other pending applications. Do I need a business plan to apply for grants in Florida? Most quality grant applications ask for a business plan or summary, especially for funding over $10,000. This does not always need to be formal, but it should outline your objectives, timeline, market, and how funds will be used. Strong plans significantly boost your approval odds. Are there grants for veteran-owned businesses in Florida? Several grants and technical assistance programs are geared toward veteran entrepreneurs. These are often supported by federal or state partnerships or local Chambers of Commerce. You may need DD-214 documentation and a majority veteran ownership stake. # Business Grants

## Looking for Even More Reasons?

The Miami Downtown Development Authority (Miami DDA) is the economic development agency for the City of Miami’s urban core and maintains several concentrations, including Advocacy, Enhanced Services, Urban Planning, Marketing & Communications, and Business Development. Together we work to fulfill our mission statement “to grow, strengthen and promote the economic health and vitality of Downtown Miami”.

The Business Development team focuses explicitly on the retention and recruitment of both businesses and talent, with a high emphasis on the Technology and Finance industries. Our team also works closely with ownership groups and their representatives to recruit new-to-market companies to Downtown Miami.  the services provided assist them both before and after their arrival.  These efforts include incentive packages, research assistance, joint presentations, permitting assistance, introductions to key stakeholders, exposure, and more.

Thank you for taking an interest in the City of Miami, and specifically within our urban core. Whether you are a company or an individual considering the move, or if you already have, we welcome you to a brighter future.

## Miami DDA Business Incentive Grants

The Miami Downtown Development Authority is fueling Downtown Miami’s economic boom by offering grants to businesses relocating or expanding within its vibrant districts. Grants are available for ground-floor retail, ground-floor food & beverage establishments, tech start-ups and mid-sized businesses. Join us in shaping the future of Downtown Miami’s business landscape.

- [Miami DDA Incentive Programs One Pager(PDF, 3MB)](https://www.miamidda.com/files/assets/miamidda/v/1/business-development/documents/doing-business-in-downtown-miami/incetive_program_all_programs.pdf "Incetive_program_all_programs.pdf")
- [Business Welcome Packet(PDF, 20MB)](https://www.miamidda.com/files/assets/miamidda/v/1/grants-amp-services/documents/business_welcome_package_072524.pdf)

## Property Improvement Grant Program

The Property Improvement Grant Program provides grant funding for qualified exterior improvements. The program’s goal is to improve the central business district’s physical environment (“curb appeal”) and enhance the area’s overall perception – while supporting increased economic activity and investment. The program is designed to attract and retain retail businesses and restaurants while growing the customer base for area businesses.

The Property Improvement Grant Program is funded by the Miami Downtown Development Authority (Miami DDA) and administered by the Downtown Miami Partnership (DMP). All applications are reviewed by an independent committee that awards funds at its discretion – and in accordance with the program guidelines.

- [Property Improvement Grant Program Guidelines(PDF, 201KB)](https://www.miamidda.com/files/assets/miamidda/v/1/business-development/documents/202021-property-improvement-grant-program-guidelines.pdf)
- [Property Improvement Grant Program Application(PDF, 485KB)](https://www.miamidda.com/files/assets/miamidda/v/1/business-development/documents/202021-property-improvement-grant-application.pdf)

## Business Development Resources

**[Guide to Opening a Business in The City of Miami](https://www.miami.gov/Business-Licenses/Business-Licensing/Guide-to-Opening-a-Business-in-The-City-of-Miami)**

The main two items you need from The City in order to open a business in Miami are (in order): Certificate of Use and a Business Tax Receipt.

**[Miami-Dade County Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources](https://www.miamidade.gov/global/economy/home.page)**

The Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources provides information for businesses, licensing, available business incentives and permitting – along with planning and zoning. View more detailed information on these services, starting a business, small business development and much more.

**[The Beacon Council](https://www.beaconcouncil.com/)**

Serving as Miami-Dade County’s official economic development partnership, The Beacon Council is charged with bringing new job-generating investments to the community – while assisting existing businesses in expansion efforts.

**[Enterprise Florida](https://selectflorida.org/)**

As the State of Florida’s Economic Development Agency, Enterprise Florida, Inc. (EFI) serves as a public-private partnership between Florida’s businesses and government leaders. Enterprise Florida’s mission is to expand and diversify the state’s economy through job creation.

**[U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA)](https://www.sba.gov/)**

U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) can provide valuable training, access to finance, and assistance with government contracting. # Grant Opportunities

The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services offers a variety of federal and state grant opportunities. Each opportunity is unique to the specific division identified and can include various award criteria. To view active or available grant opportunities, visit [FDACS Grant Opportunities](https://grants.fdacs.gov/ "https://grants.fdacs.gov/").

Filter by keyword:

Filter Search

### [Community Forest Program](https://www.fdacs.gov/Forest-Wildfire/Our-Forests/Land-Planning-and-Administration/Community-Forest-Program "")

This grant program helps conserve land and establish community forests that provide continuing and accessible community benefits.

### [FDACS Applied Mosquito Control Research](https://www.fdacs.gov/Business-Services/Mosquito-Control/FDACS-Applied-Mosquito-Control-Research "")

This grant program is for mosquito control applied and basic research into the practical methods of control that can be used by local mosquito control agencies.

### [Florida Retail Fuel Transfer Switch Modernization Grant Program](https://www.fdacs.gov/Business-Services/Grant-Opportunities/Florida-Retail-Fuel-Transfer-Switch-Modernization-Grant-Program "")

This program offers financial aid to retail fuel facilities for the installation or modernization of transfer switch infrastructure.

### [Florida Specialty Crop Block Grant Program](https://fdacs.my.site.com/fdacsgrants/s/ "")

The purpose of the Specialty Crop Block Grant Program is to enhance the competitiveness of specialty crops.

### [Florida Specialty Crop Multi-State Program](https://fdacs.my.site.com/fdacsgrants/s/ "")

This program funds collaborative, multi-state projects that address food safety, plant pests and diseases, and other specialty crop issues.

### [Florida Urban and Community Forestry Grants](https://www.fdacs.gov/Forest-Wildfire/For-Communities/Urban-Forestry/Florida-Urban-and-Community-Forestry-Grants "")

This program makes funds available to organizations to develop or enhance their urban and community forestry programs.

### [Florida's Future Forests Program](https://www.fdacs.gov/Forest-Wildfire/For-Landowners/Grants/Florida-s-Future-Forests-Program "")

This program is designed to help increase the acreage of healthy forests in Florida.

### [Food, Nutrition and Wellness Grants](https://www.fdacs.gov/Business-Services/Grant-Opportunities/Food-Nutrition-and-Wellness-Grants "")

Locate grants to assist with nutrition education, equipment, school gardens and more.

### [Southern Pine Beetle Assistance and Prevention Program](https://www.fdacs.gov/Forest-Wildfire/For-Landowners/Programs-for-Landowners/Southern-Pine-Beetle-Assistance-and-Prevention-Program "")

This program helps landowners conduct management practices that can make their pine stands less susceptible to southern pine beetles.

### [USDA Grants](https://www.grants.gov/ "")

Qualified Florida agribusinesses could benefit from grant opportunities offered throughout the year by the U.S. Department of Agriculture.

### [Volunteer Fire Assistance Grants](https://www.fdacs.gov/Forest-Wildfire/For-Communities/Grants/Volunteer-Fire-Assistance-Grants "")

This program provides assistance to state foresters to organize, train and equip fire departments in rural areas.

[![sbi-banner](https://floridajobs.org/images/default-source/homepage-sliders/sbi-banner.jpg?sfvrsn=f3ee5cb0_0)](https://cloud.communications.deo.myflorida.com/newsandinfo)

FloridaCommerce Office of Small Business Innovation promotes economic prosperity for Florida's small businesses through economic development programs to further diversify Florida's economy and create future resiliency.

These programs provide newly established or growing small businesses with access to capital, technical assistance and business management training to small business owners to foster vibrant and healthy communities.

FloridaCommerce administers various loan programs available to eligible small businesses in Florida and works with strategic partners to assist small businesses in efficiently operating, expanding and creating jobs for hardworking Florida families. Administration includes overseeing and monitoring of all development financing programs and providing technical assistance and support to small businesses.

## Business Advantages

- Increases access to affordable long-term capital without the high down payment requirements often associated with conventional financing programs;
- Includes eligibility for newly established or growing small businesses;
- Offers flexible use of funds - startup costs, working capital and the acquisition of real estate and other major fixed assets; and
- Provides business management training and technical assistance.

## Lender Advantages

- Expands your business loan portfolio;
- Minimizes collateral risk and puts your lending organization in a first lien position with an attractive 50% LTV;
- Lending organization makes its own credit decisions with its own loan documentation;
- Earns fees and interest income on interim loans related to the project;
- Helps manage lending limits and industry exposure; and
- Streamlines procedures and quick response to project loan requests.

## Learn More About the Small Business Innovation Loan Programs

### [Rebuild Florida Business Loan Fund](https://floridajobs.org/business-growth-and-partnerships/Small-and-Minority-Business-Resources/Small-Business-Innovation\#)

The [Rebuild Florida Business Loan Fund](https://floridajobs.org/business-growth-and-partnerships/Small-and-Minority-Business-Resources/Small-Business-Innovation/rebuild-florida-business-loan-fund) is a program created to provide financing to assist businesses with resiliency efforts. The funds will address the current gap in available, affordable capital for businesses that can be used for inventory purchases, construction, working capital, equipment financing and more.

### [Florida Small Business Emergency Bridge Loan](https://floridajobs.org/business-growth-and-partnerships/Small-and-Minority-Business-Resources/Small-Business-Innovation\#)

The [Florida Small Business Emergency Bridge Loan Program](https://floridacommerce.my.site.com/RebuildFloridaBusinessLoanFund/s/) provides short-term, interest-free working capital loans that are intended to "bridge the gap" between the time a major catastrophe hits and when a business has secured longer term recovery resources.

### [Rural Community Development Revolving Loan Program](https://floridajobs.org/business-growth-and-partnerships/Small-and-Minority-Business-Resources/Small-Business-Innovation\#)

The [Rural Community Development Revolving Loan Program](https://floridajobs.org/business-growth-and-partnerships/Small-and-Minority-Business-Resources/Small-Business-Innovation/rural-community-development-revolving-loan-program) provides financial assistance to local governments in the form of a loan or loan guaranty for projects that will maintain or create new jobs and increase the economic vitality and diversification of Florida's rural counties and communities. The program provides loans for uses such as the purchase of equipment; the acquisition, construction or improvement of buildings; and acquisition of land and water/sewer projects.

### [State Small Business Credit Initiative](https://floridajobs.org/business-growth-and-partnerships/Small-and-Minority-Business-Resources/Small-Business-Innovation\#)

Originally created in 2010 and reauthorized as part of the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, the [State Small Business Credit Initiative](https://floridajobs.org/FloridaSSBCI) (SSBCI) allocates funding through the United States Department of the Treasury (Treasury) to states for their own capital access initiatives. In the coming months, FloridaCommerce will submit a plan to the Treasury that details how Florida will utilize SSBCI funds to provide access to capital for targeted small business population(s).

More information will be available pending guidance from the Treasury.

### [Microfinance Guarantee Program](https://floridajobs.org/business-growth-and-partnerships/Small-and-Minority-Business-Resources/Small-Business-Innovation\#)

The purpose of the [Microfinance Guarantee Program](https://floridajobs.org/business-growth-and-partnerships/Small-and-Minority-Business-Resources/Small-Business-Innovation/microfinance-guarantee-program) is to improve the ability of entrepreneurs and small businesses to access capital offering loan guarantees to lenders that extend credit.

### [Black Business Loan Program](https://floridajobs.org/business-growth-and-partnerships/Small-and-Minority-Business-Resources/Small-Business-Innovation\#)

The [Black Business Loan Program](https://floridajobs.org/business-growth-and-partnerships/Small-and-Minority-Business-Resources/Small-Business-Innovation/black-business-loan-program) offers alternative lending solutions to Florida-based black owned small businesses by providing short-term loans and technical assistance.

### [Prospera](https://floridajobs.org/business-growth-and-partnerships/Small-and-Minority-Business-Resources/Small-Business-Innovation\#)

[Prospera](https://prosperausa.org/) provides technical assistance and financial education to Hispanic-owned businesses and entrepreneurs.

### [Urban League of Broward County](https://floridajobs.org/business-growth-and-partnerships/Small-and-Minority-Business-Resources/Small-Business-Innovation\#)

The [Urban League of Broward County](http://www.cccdcorp.org/) provides technical assistance and capital to entrepreneurs and minority-owned businesses.
